bodies.name: Sun
bodies.explorationHistory: Parker Solar Probe, SOHO, SDO, Ulysses, Solar Orbiter, Helios.
bodies.notes: Added for the 3D scene; not present in the workbook.

bodies.name: Mercury
bodies.atmosphere: Almost none — a thin exosphere of oxygen, sodium, hydrogen, helium and potassium
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 0.466 AU (69.7 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 250.4deg, and about 1.248 AU from Earth
bodies.explorationHistory: Mariner 10, MESSENGER, BepiColombo (en route); known since prehistory and first visited by Mariner 10 in 1974
bodies.notes: Closest planet to the Sun and the smallest in the Solar System. Its day (176 Earth days) lasts two of its years; it has a huge iron core making up ~85% of its radius and water ice hidden in permanently shadowed polar craters.

bodies.name: Venus
bodies.atmosphere: 96.5% carbon dioxide, 3.5% nitrogen, sulphuric acid clouds
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 0.727 AU (108.8 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 343.7deg, and about 0.384 AU from Earth
bodies.explorationHistory: Mariner 2, Venera 1-16, Pioneer Venus, Magellan, Venus Express, Akatsuki; known since prehistory and first visited by Mariner 2 in 1962
bodies.notes: The hottest planet, with a runaway greenhouse effect and surface pressure 92 times Earth's. It rotates backwards and so slowly that a Venusian day is longer than its year. Its clouds are made of sulphuric acid.

bodies.name: Earth
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 1.003 AU (150.1 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 1.4deg, and about 0.000 AU from Earth
bodies.explorationHistory: Continuously observed; first flyby by Luna 1 (1959) and first orbit by Luna 10 (1966)
bodies.notes: The only known world with life and liquid surface water. Its large Moon stabilises its axial tilt, and its magnetic field shields it from the solar wind.

bodies.name: Mars
bodies.atmosphere: 95% carbon dioxide, 2.8% nitrogen, 2% argon, traces of oxygen
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 1.550 AU (231.9 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 82.2deg, and about 1.706 AU from Earth
bodies.explorationHistory: Mariner 4 (1965), Viking 1 and 2 (1976), and more than 50 subsequent missions
bodies.notes: Home to Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the Solar System (21.9 km), and Valles Marineris, a canyon system over 4,000 km long. Evidence shows it once had rivers and lakes.

bodies.name: Jupiter
bodies.atmosphere: 90% hydrogen, 10% helium, traces of methane and ammonia
bodies.notableMoons: Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto (plus 93 smaller moons in the IAU list)
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 5.304 AU (793.5 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 130.6deg, and about 5.989 AU from Earth
bodies.explorationHistory: Pioneer 10 (1973), Voyager 1 and 2 (1979), Galileo (1995-2003), Cassini flyby (2000), Juno (2016-present), JUICE and Europa Clipper (en route); known since prehistory and its moons were discovered by Galileo in 1610
bodies.notes: The largest planet — more massive than all other planets combined. Its Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth that has raged for centuries, and its moon Ganymede is the largest moon in the Solar System.

bodies.name: Saturn
bodies.ringSystem: Yes — the most extensive ring system, 282,000 km across
bodies.notableMoons: Titan, Enceladus, Mimas, Tethys, Dione, Rhea, Iapetus, Hyperion, Phoebe
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 9.444 AU (1412.8 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 10.5deg, and about 8.456 AU from Earth
bodies.explorationHistory: Pioneer 11 (1979), Voyager 1 and 2 (1980-81), Cassini-Huygens (2004-2017); known since prehistory and its rings were first seen by Galileo in 1610
bodies.notes: Its rings are made almost entirely of water ice and are only tens of metres thick. Titan has a thick nitrogen atmosphere and methane lakes, and Enceladus shoots water plumes from a subsurface ocean.

bodies.name: Uranus
bodies.notableMoons: Miranda, Ariel, Umbriel, Titania, Oberon, Puck
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 19.440 AU (2908.2 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 63.6deg, and about 18.993 AU from Earth
bodies.notes: The coldest planetary atmosphere in the Solar System, with a minimum of -224°C. Its extreme 98° axial tilt means it effectively orbits on its side, giving 42-year-long days and nights at the poles.

bodies.name: Neptune
bodies.ringSystem: Yes — faint rings and ring arcs
bodies.notableMoons: Triton, Nereid, Proteus, Naiad, Thalassa, Despina, Galatea, Larissa
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 29.877 AU (4469.6 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 1.9deg, and about 28.874 AU from Earth
bodies.notes: The windiest world known, with speeds reaching 2,100 km/h. It was discovered by mathematics before it was seen: Le Verrier predicted its position from irregularities in Uranus's orbit, and it was found within a degree of the prediction in 1846.

bodies.name: Pluto
bodies.atmosphere: Thin nitrogen, methane and carbon monoxide atmosphere
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 35.614 AU (5327.8 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 304.2deg, and about 35.083 AU from Earth
bodies.explorationHistory: New Horizons (14 July 2015) — the only visit
bodies.notes: Reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006. It has a huge nitrogen-ice glacier shaped like a heart (Sputnik Planitia) and a surprisingly active surface, and it is locked in a binary dance with Charon.

bodies.name: Ceres
bodies.atmosphere: Transient water vapour, no significant atmosphere
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 2.805 AU (419.6 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 258.8deg, and about 3.178 AU from Earth
bodies.explorationHistory: Dawn (2015-2018); discovered by Giuseppe Piazzi on 1 January 1801 — the first asteroid found
bodies.notes: The largest object in the asteroid belt and the only dwarf planet in the inner Solar System. Bright carbonate deposits on its surface point to a briny subsurface reservoir.

bodies.name: Eris
bodies.atmosphere: Frozen methane and nitrogen surface; no significant atmosphere
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 96.167 AU (14386.4 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 23.6deg, and about 95.258 AU from Earth
bodies.notes: An extremely distant world whose discovery in 2005 (and its greater mass than Pluto) directly forced the 2006 redefinition of "planet". It is currently near aphelion.

bodies.name: Haumea
bodies.ringSystem: Yes — a narrow ring discovered in 2017
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 50.102 AU (7495.1 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 207.7deg, and about 50.899 AU from Earth
bodies.notes: One of the fastest-spinning large bodies known (a 3.9-hour day), which has stretched it into an ellipsoid. It also has a ring, making it the first known dwarf planet with one.

bodies.name: Makemake
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 52.490 AU (7852.4 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 175.5deg, and about 53.366 AU from Earth
bodies.notes: A reddish Kuiper Belt world with a highly reflective methane-frost surface and one dark moon. It was discovered in 2005.

bodies.name: Gonggong
bodies.positionSummary: Position not computed for this body
bodies.notes: A large, slow-rotating reddish world beyond Pluto whose discovery supported the existence of a distant "Planet Nine". A ring was discovered around it in 2025.

bodies.name: Quaoar
bodies.ringSystem: Yes — a ring outside the Roche limit
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 45.235 AU (6767.1 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 131.2deg, and about 45.879 AU from Earth
bodies.notes: Famous for having a ring that orbits farther out than the Roche limit, which was long thought impossible — a puzzle for ring formation theories.

bodies.name: Sedna
bodies.positionSummary: At 2026-09-24 20:14 UTC: about 85.244 AU (12752.3 million km) from the Sun, at heliocentric ecliptic longitude 50.3deg, and about 84.601 AU from Earth
bodies.notes: One of the most distant known Solar System objects, on a 11,400-year orbit that never comes closer than 76 AU to the Sun. Its 2014 discovery hinted at a distant unseen planet.

bodies.name: Moon
bodies.atmosphere: Almost none — a thin exosphere of helium, neon, hydrogen and argon
bodies.positionSummary: Orbits Earth every 27.3 days, 384,400 km away; the only other world humans have walked on.
bodies.explorationHistory: Luna program, Ranger and Surveyor, Apollo 11-17 (12 crewed landings and 6 landings), Lunokhod, Chang'e, Chandrayaan, LRO, LCROSS, SLIM, Artemis.
bodies.notes: Added as a first-class body so the 55 Moon-targeted missions have a destination in the 3D scene.

bodies.explorationHistory: Dawn, Hayabusa2, OSIRIS-REx, Rosetta, Deep Impact, Stardust, NEAR Shoemaker, DART, Lucy, Psyche.
bodies.notes: Synthetic scene anchor for asteroid and comet targets.
bodies.atmosphere: Not applicable — these are small bodies
