missions.name: Mariner 10
missions.currentLocation: Heliocentric orbit, now a derelict spacecraft circling the Sun
missions.story: First spacecraft to visit Mercury and the first to use a gravity assist from another planet (Venus). It flew past Mercury three times, photographing about 45% of the surface.
missions.achievement: Discovered Mercury's weak magnetic field and large iron core; first close-up images of Mercury; proved gravity-assist navigation.

missions.name: MESSENGER
missions.currentLocation: Deliberately impacted Mercury's surface near Shakespeare crater
missions.story: MErcury Surface, Space ENvironment, GEochemistry and Ranging. First spacecraft to orbit Mercury (2011), completing 4,105 orbits over four years.
missions.achievement: Mapped 100% of Mercury in colour; confirmed water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters; found a large, offset magnetic field and unexpected volcanism.

missions.name: BepiColombo
missions.currentLocation: Heliocentric orbit in final approach to Mercury; orbit insertion scheduled late 2026
missions.story: Europe's first mission to Mercury, carrying ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (Mio). Using nine planetary flybys to brake into orbit.
missions.achievement: Completed six Mercury flybys (last on 8 Jan 2025); delivered the first mid-infrared measurements of Mercury's surface; discovered escaping ions and unexpected surface features.

missions.name: Venera 1
missions.story: The first spacecraft ever launched toward another planet. Contact was lost en route, most likely due to a guidance failure.
missions.achievement: First man-made object placed on a heliocentric transfer orbit to another planet.

missions.name: Mariner 2
missions.story: The first successful planetary encounter in history, passing 34,773 km from Venus after a 109-day cruise.
missions.achievement: Measured Venus's surface temperature (~425°C) and confirmed a dense CO2 atmosphere, ruling out liquid water and ending speculation about a habitable Venus.

missions.name: Venera 4
missions.currentLocation: Destroyed by atmospheric pressure ~25 km altitude
missions.story: The first probe to transmit data from inside another planet's atmosphere, reporting for 93 minutes while descending by parachute.
missions.achievement: First direct in-situ measurement of another planet's atmosphere; found ~90-95% CO2 with almost no oxygen or water vapour.

missions.name: Venera 5
missions.story: Follow-up atmospheric probe that transmitted for 53 minutes before being crushed.
missions.achievement: Confirmed Venera 4's CO2-dominated atmosphere and measured higher pressures than expected.

missions.name: Venera 6
missions.story: Twin of Venera 5 with a stronger pressure vessel; returned 51 minutes of data.
missions.achievement: Refined the measured atmospheric composition and pressure profile.

missions.name: Venera 7
missions.currentLocation: Landed on Venus surface, now extinct at approximately 5°S, 351°E
missions.story: The first spacecraft to soft-land on another planet and transmit data from its surface, surviving 23 minutes in 465°C heat.
missions.achievement: Measured surface temperature ~475°C and pressure ~90 atmospheres; first data transmitted from the surface of another world.

missions.name: Venera 8
missions.story: Survived 50 minutes on the surface and measured the composition of the crust.
missions.achievement: First analysis of another planet's surface rock (granite-like) and measurement of near-surface light levels.

missions.name: Venera 9
missions.story: First spacecraft to orbit Venus and the first to return photographs from the surface of another planet (black and white, 180° panorama).
missions.achievement: First images from Venus's surface; measured wind speeds and cloud structure; discovered a layered cloud deck.

missions.name: Venera 10
missions.story: Second successful Venus surface landing in the same launch window, returning a 174° panorama.
missions.achievement: Confirmed the pancake-like volcanic rock terrain of the Venera 9 site.

missions.name: Venera 11
missions.story: Lander reached the surface and transmitted for 95 minutes, but its camera and soil analyser failed.
missions.achievement: Detected lightning and measured atmospheric composition including the first detection of carbon monoxide in Venus's lower atmosphere.

missions.name: Venera 12
missions.story: Twin of Venera 11 with a similar partial success on the surface.
missions.achievement: Recorded a burst of lightning and measured surface temperature and pressure.

missions.name: Pioneer Venus Orbiter
missions.currentLocation: Decayed into Venus's atmosphere in October 1992
missions.story: Orbited Venus for 14 years, the longest continuous Venus survey, using radar to map the surface through the clouds.
missions.achievement: First global radar map of Venus; discovered the high-altitude "ionotail"; monitored the atmosphere for over a decade.

missions.name: Pioneer Venus Multiprobe
missions.story: Dropped one large and three small probes into Venus's atmosphere at different locations simultaneously.
missions.achievement: First multi-point simultaneous atmospheric profile of another planet; one probe survived the impact and transmitted briefly from the surface.

missions.name: Venera 13
missions.story: Returned the first colour photographs of the Venusian surface and survived 127 minutes, a record for the Venera programme.
missions.achievement: First colour images from Venus; first X-ray fluorescence analysis of Venusian soil, finding basaltic rock.

missions.name: Venera 14
missions.story: Twin of Venera 13, landing four days later and returning colour panoramas plus soil data.
missions.achievement: Confirmed basaltic crust and measured compressibility of the surface material; recorded 57 minutes on the surface.

missions.name: Venera 15
missions.story: Radar-mapped the northern hemisphere of Venus from orbit at high resolution.
missions.achievement: Produced detailed radar maps that revealed large volcanic structures and the oldest terrain on Venus.

missions.name: Venera 16
missions.story: Companion radar mapper covering the remaining northern latitudes.
missions.achievement: Completed a detailed radar atlas of the northern quarter of Venus.

missions.name: Vega 1
missions.story: Released a balloon into Venus's atmosphere and a lander, then continued to a Comet Halley flyby.
missions.achievement: First balloon flight in another planet's atmosphere (46 hours of data); measured Halley's dust and gas.

missions.name: Vega 2
missions.story: Second Venus balloon plus a closer Halley encounter at 8,030 km on 9 March 1986.
missions.achievement: Second atmospheric balloon; returned detailed comet nucleus images and dust measurements.

missions.name: Magellan
missions.story: Used synthetic aperture radar to map 98% of Venus's surface at high resolution over four years.
missions.achievement: Produced the definitive global radar map of Venus; found evidence of recent volcanism and no plate tectonics.

missions.name: Venus Express
missions.currentLocation: Decayed into Venus's atmosphere, likely burned up in 2015
missions.story: Europe's first Venus orbiter, studying the atmosphere, plasma environment and surface from polar orbit.
missions.achievement: Detected hydroxyl in the atmosphere, mapped wind patterns, found volcanic hot spots and confirmed lightning.

missions.name: Akatsuki
missions.currentLocation: Heliocentric orbit after contact was lost
missions.story: Also known as Planet-C. Survived an orbit-insertion failure in 2010 and entered Venus orbit in 2015 using a five-year backup plan.
missions.achievement: First successful Japanese Venus orbiter; discovered strong equatorial jet winds and studied Venusian lightning and cloud dynamics for nine years.

missions.name: VERITAS
missions.story: Venus Emissivity, Radio Science, InSAR, Topography and Spectroscopy — a radar mapper to study Venus's surface and interior.
missions.achievement: Planned: high-resolution global radar maps, gravity field and near-infrared emissivity mapping.

missions.name: DAVINCI
missions.story: Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry and Imaging — a descent probe to measure Venus's atmosphere and take the first descent images since 1985.
missions.achievement: Planned: precise noble-gas and isotope measurements to determine Venus's history.

missions.name: Shukrayaan-1
missions.story: India's first Venus mission, planned to study the surface, atmosphere and solar wind interaction.
missions.achievement: Planned: radar and atmospheric studies of Venus.

missions.name: Luna 1
missions.story: First spacecraft to leave Earth's orbit and reach the vicinity of the Moon; missed the Moon and entered heliocentric orbit.
missions.achievement: Discovered the solar wind and the absence of a lunar magnetic field.

missions.name: Luna 2
missions.currentLocation: Impacted the Moon near Mare Imbrium (about 29.1°N, 0°W)
missions.story: Became the first human-made object to reach the surface of another celestial body.
missions.achievement: Detected no magnetic field and no radiation belts around the Moon.

missions.name: Luna 3
missions.story: Returned the first photographs of the Moon's far side, which had never been seen from Earth.
missions.achievement: First images of the lunar far side; revealed a different, less maria-rich terrain and led to naming far-side features.

missions.name: Ranger 7
missions.story: First fully successful US lunar mission, transmitting 4,316 close-up images in the final 17 minutes before impact.
missions.achievement: Set the standard for lunar surface imaging and site selection for Apollo.

missions.name: Ranger 8
missions.story: Returned 7,137 images of the Sea of Tranquility before impact.
missions.achievement: Provided detailed topography for the future Apollo 11 landing site.

missions.name: Ranger 9
missions.story: Returned 5,814 images of Alphonsus crater, the last of the Ranger series.
missions.achievement: Live television from the Moon; confirmed cratered terrain for Apollo planning.

missions.name: Luna 9
missions.story: Achieved the first survivable soft landing on the Moon and transmitted the first photographs from its surface.
missions.achievement: First soft landing on any celestial body; proved the surface could support a lander, ending fears of deep dust.

missions.name: Luna 10
missions.story: First spacecraft to enter orbit around the Moon.
missions.achievement: First lunar orbital data on gravity, radiation and micrometeoroids; discovered mascons indirectly through gravity studies.

missions.name: Surveyor 1
missions.story: First US soft landing on the Moon, returning 11,237 images and proving the surface was firm.
missions.achievement: Confirmed a bearing strength suitable for crewed landings; first US images from the lunar surface.

missions.name: Surveyor 3
missions.story: Landed and dug trenches with a scoop; famously later visited by Apollo 12 astronauts who retrieved its camera.
missions.achievement: Demonstrated soil mechanics on the Moon; its retrieved parts showed the effects of 2.5 years of lunar exposure.

missions.name: Lunar Orbiter 1
missions.currentLocation: Deliberately crashed on the far side
missions.story: First US spacecraft to orbit the Moon; photographed potential Apollo landing sites and returned the first image of Earth from lunar distance.
missions.achievement: First photograph of Earth from the Moon; mapped 99% of the Moon.

missions.name: Zond 5
missions.currentLocation: Returned to Earth and splashed down in the Indian Ocean
missions.story: First spacecraft to travel around the Moon and return to Earth, carrying turtles, flies, plants and bacteria.
missions.achievement: First living organisms to return from the vicinity of the Moon; a Soviet step toward a crewed lunar flyby.

missions.name: Apollo 8
missions.currentLocation: Crew returned safely; spacecraft burned up on re-entry
missions.story: First crewed mission to leave Earth orbit, orbit the Moon and return. Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders made 10 lunar orbits.
missions.achievement: First humans to see the far side and Earthrise; the iconic "Earthrise" photograph changed public perception of Earth.

missions.name: Apollo 11
missions.story: First crewed landing on the Moon. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed the Eagle in the Sea of Tranquility on 20 July 1969 while Michael Collins orbited above.
missions.achievement: First humans on another world; returned 21.5 kg of samples and deployed a seismometer, laser reflector and solar wind collector.

missions.name: Apollo 12
missions.story: Precision landing near the Surveyor 3 probe, proving pinpoint navigation; the launch was struck by lightning twice and recovered.
missions.achievement: Retrieved parts of Surveyor 3; deployed the first Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package and returned 34 kg of samples.

missions.name: Apollo 13
missions.currentLocation: Command module returned to Earth; lunar module burned up in Earth's atmosphere
missions.story: An oxygen tank explosion crippled the spacecraft en route; the crew used the lunar module as a lifeboat and looped around the Moon to return.
missions.achievement: "Successful failure" — all three astronauts survived; demonstrated extraordinary mission control problem-solving.

missions.name: Apollo 14
missions.story: Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell landed in the Fra Mauro highlands; Shepard famously hit two golf balls on the Moon.
missions.achievement: Returned 42 kg of samples including the "Big Bertha" rock; extensive seismic and geological work.

missions.name: Apollo 15
missions.story: First "J-mission" with the Lunar Roving Vehicle, enabling far longer traverses in the Hadley-Apennine region.
missions.achievement: First lunar rover use; returned the "Genesis Rock", ancient anorthosite from the lunar highlands.

missions.name: Apollo 16
missions.story: First landing in the lunar highlands (Descartes), with three rover traverses totalling 26.7 km.
missions.achievement: Returned 95.7 kg of samples, the heaviest Apollo sample return.

missions.name: Apollo 17
missions.story: The last crewed Moon landing. Eugene Cernan and geologist Harrison Schmitt spent 75 hours on the surface in the Taurus-Littrow valley.
missions.achievement: Longest Apollo surface stay; returned 110.5 kg of samples; Schmitt was the only professional geologist to walk on the Moon.

missions.name: Luna 16
missions.currentLocation: Sample returned to Earth; lander remains in Mare Fecunditatis
missions.story: First robotic sample-return from the Moon, bringing 101 g back to Earth.
missions.achievement: Proved robotic sample return was feasible; returned mare basalt.

missions.name: Lunokhod 1
missions.story: First remote-controlled rover on another world, delivered by Luna 17. It drove 10.5 km over 322 Earth days.
missions.achievement: Returned 20,000 images and 200 panoramas; analysed lunar soil at 500 locations.

missions.name: Lunokhod 2
missions.story: Drove 39 km in four months, a record for a rover until 2014.
missions.achievement: Returned 86 panoramas and 80,000 TV images; measured soil mechanics and magnetic fields.

missions.name: Luna 24
missions.story: The last Soviet lunar mission and the last sample return until 2020, bringing back 170 g.
missions.achievement: Returned the first evidence of water-bearing minerals in lunar soil.

missions.name: Clementine
missions.currentLocation: Abandoned in geocentric orbit until 1994, then heliocentric
missions.story: Mapped the Moon globally in 11 spectral bands over two months, then attempted a flyby of asteroid 1620 Geographos (failed).
missions.achievement: First global multispectral and topographic mapping of the Moon; radar hints of polar water ice.

missions.name: Lunar Prospector
missions.currentLocation: Deliberately impacted Shoemaker crater near the south pole
missions.story: Low-cost Discovery mission that orbited the Moon in a polar orbit for 19 months.
missions.achievement: Strong evidence of hydrogen (possible water ice) at the poles; produced first global lunar gravity and magnetic maps.

missions.name: SMART-1
missions.currentLocation: Deliberately impacted the Moon (Lake of Excellence)
missions.story: Europe's first Moon mission and the first to reach the Moon using solar-electric ion propulsion.
missions.achievement: Tested ion propulsion and returned lunar surface composition maps including calcium and magnesium.

missions.name: Kaguya (SELENE)
missions.story: Japan's first lunar orbiter, carrying two small sub-satellites (Okina and Ouna) for gravity mapping.
missions.achievement: Best gravity map of the Moon at the time; high-definition imagery and a far-side gravity map.

missions.name: Chang'e 1
missions.story: China's first lunar mission, orbiting the Moon for 16 months.
missions.achievement: Produced a full lunar image map; microwave radiometry; planned impact on 1 March 2009.

missions.name: Chandrayaan-1
missions.story: India's first lunar mission, carrying a Moon Impact Probe and NASA's M3 instrument.
missions.achievement: M3 detected water molecules on the lunar surface — a landmark discovery; mapped minerals across the Moon.

missions.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO)
missions.story: Still operating after more than 15 years in lunar orbit, mapping the surface in unprecedented detail and characterising radiation.
missions.achievement: Highest-resolution lunar maps; located water ice; tracked landing sites; provided critical data for Artemis and commercial landers.

missions.name: LCROSS
missions.story: Steered the Centaur upper stage into Cabeus crater near the south pole and flew through the resulting plume.
missions.achievement: Confirmed water ice on the Moon — about 5.6% by mass in the plume.

missions.name: GRAIL
missions.currentLocation: Both deliberately impacted near the north pole
missions.story: Twins Ebb and Flow mapped the Moon's gravity field to exceptional precision.
missions.achievement: Highest-resolution gravity map of any celestial body; revealed a deeply fractured crust and ancient impact basins.

missions.name: LADEE
missions.story: Studied the lunar exosphere and dust environment from a low equatorial orbit.
missions.achievement: Characterised the dusty plasma environment; confirmed neon in the exosphere; tested a laser communication link.

missions.name: Chang'e 3
missions.currentLocation: Landed at 44.12°N, 19.51°W; lander still occasionally active
missions.story: China's first lunar soft landing, delivering the Yutu (Jade Rabbit) rover to Mare Imbrium.
missions.achievement: First soft landing on the Moon since Luna 24 in 1976; rover operated for nearly three years.

missions.name: Chang'e 4
missions.workingNowText: Yes — Yutu-2 rover and lander still operating
missions.story: First landing on the lunar far side, in the South Pole-Aitken basin, using the Queqiao relay satellite for communications.
missions.achievement: First far-side soft landing in history; Yutu-2 rover has driven more than 1.6 km.

missions.name: Chang'e 5
missions.story: Returned 1,731 g of lunar samples, ending a 44-year gap in lunar sample return.
missions.achievement: Youngest lunar samples ever returned; found a new mineral (Changesite-(Y)).

missions.name: Chang'e 6
missions.story: First sample return from the lunar far side, landing in the Apollo crater within the South Pole-Aitken basin.
missions.achievement: Returned 1,935 g of far-side material, enabling comparison of the Moon's two hemispheres.

missions.name: Beresheet
missions.story: First privately funded lunar lander and first Israeli lunar attempt, built on the Google Lunar XPRIZE legacy.
missions.achievement: Reached lunar orbit but crashed during descent; carried a lunar library archive.

missions.name: Chandrayaan-2
missions.story: Orbiter successful; the Vikram lander crashed during its final descent in September 2019.
missions.achievement: Orbiter continues to map the Moon and detected argon-40 and lunar hydroxyl; lander failure drove the redesign behind Chandrayaan-3.

missions.name: Chandrayaan-3
missions.workingNowText: Lander/rover dormant after the lunar night (not expected to wake)
missions.story: First landing near the lunar south pole (69.37°S) and India's first lunar soft landing.
missions.achievement: First-ever south-pole landing; Pragyan rover measured plasma and confirmed sulphur and other elements; a "hop" test proved re-launch capability.

missions.name: SLIM
missions.workingNowText: No (lost power, entered dormant state, no further contact)
missions.story: Smart Lander for Investigating Moon achieved a precision landing within about 55 m of its target.
missions.achievement: Japan became the fifth nation to soft-land on the Moon; first precision ("pinpoint") lunar landing.

missions.name: Luna 25
missions.story: Russia's first lunar mission since 1976, aiming for the south pole near Boguslawsky crater.
missions.achievement: Crashed during the orbit-lowering burn before landing.

missions.name: Artemis I
missions.currentLocation: Orion splashed down in the Pacific; upper stage in heliocentric orbit
missions.story: First integrated flight of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft, an uncrewed 25.5-day mission around the Moon.
missions.achievement: Farthest any human-rated spacecraft has travelled from Earth (432,210 km); validated heat shield and re-entry (with noted char loss).

missions.name: CAPSTONE
missions.currentLocation: Near-rectilinear halo orbit around the Moon
missions.story: A 25 kg CubeSat validating the near-rectilinear halo orbit planned for the Lunar Gateway.
missions.achievement: First CubeSat to operate at the Moon; demonstrated the NRHO for Gateway.

missions.name: Danuri (KPLO)
missions.story: Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter, South Korea's first Moon mission, carrying NASA's ShadowCam.
missions.achievement: Mapped permanently shadowed regions; first Korean deep-space mission.

missions.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
missions.workingNowText: No (ceased operations after lunar sunset, 16 March 2025)
missions.story: Commercial lunar lander that completed a full 14-day lunar day of surface operations in Mare Crisium under NASA's CLPS programme.
missions.achievement: Completed all 10 NASA payload objectives; captured a lunar eclipse and sunset imagery; landed in Mare Crisium (18.56°N, 61.81°E).

missions.name: IM-1 Odysseus
missions.story: First commercial spacecraft to soft-land on the Moon, though it tipped over on landing.
missions.achievement: First US soft landing since Apollo 17 (1972); returned the first commercial lunar surface images.

missions.name: IM-2 Athena
missions.story: Second Intuitive Machines lander targeting the lunar south pole with a drill, hopper and rover.
missions.achievement: Reached the surface near Mons Mouton but tipped over in a crater and lost power.

missions.name: Peregrine Mission 1
missions.story: First CLPS mission, which suffered a propellant valve failure shortly after launch.
missions.achievement: Collected useful data on the failure; re-entered and burned up over the Pacific.

missions.name: Hakuto-R Mission 2 (Resilience)
missions.story: Second ispace lunar landing attempt carrying a micro-rover and a water-electrolysis payload.
missions.achievement: A laser rangefinder fault caused a hard landing in Mare Frigoris.

missions.name: Artemis II
missions.story: First crewed flight of the Artemis programme; four astronauts will fly around the Moon in a free-return trajectory.
missions.achievement: Planned: first humans beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17.

missions.name: Lunar Gateway
missions.story: A small station in near-rectilinear halo orbit around the Moon to support Artemis surface missions and deep-space research.
missions.achievement: Planned: halo orbit station with Power and Propulsion Element and HALO module.

missions.name: Mariner 4
missions.story: First successful flyby of Mars, returning 21 images from 9,846 km.
missions.achievement: First close-up images of Mars — a cratered, Moon-like surface, dashing hopes of a lush planet; first radio occultation of another planet's atmosphere.

missions.name: Mariner 6
missions.story: Returned 75 images during a flyby at 3,431 km while its twin Mariner 7 approached the southern hemisphere.
missions.achievement: Analysed the atmosphere and found a thin CO2 atmosphere with surface pressure under 1% of Earth's.

missions.name: Mariner 7
missions.story: Flew within 3,430 km of Mars, imaging the southern hemisphere and the Hellas basin.
missions.achievement: First images of Mars's southern hemisphere and south polar cap.

missions.name: Mariner 9
missions.currentLocation: Decayed into the Martian atmosphere around 2022
missions.story: Became the first spacecraft to orbit another planet on 14 November 1971, arriving during a global dust storm.
missions.achievement: Mapped 85% of Mars, revealing Olympus Mons, Valles Marineris and giant volcanoes; first detailed images of Phobos and Deimos.

missions.name: Mars 2
missions.story: Orbiter succeeded (362 orbits). The lander became the first human-made object to reach the Martian surface but crashed.
missions.achievement: First object to reach Mars's surface; the attached PrOP-M would have been the first Mars rover.

missions.name: Mars 3
missions.story: Achieved the first soft landing on Mars on 2 December 1971, but the lander transmitted for only about 20 seconds.
missions.achievement: First (brief) data from the Martian surface; the failure was likely due to the global dust storm.

missions.name: Viking 1
missions.story: First fully successful Mars landing, on 20 July 1976 in Chryse Planitia. The lander operated for 2,307 Earth days.
missions.achievement: First images from the Martian surface; first life-detection experiments (results still debated); atmospheric and seismic data.

missions.name: Viking 2
missions.story: Second Viking landing, on 3 September 1976 at Utopia Planitia, operating 1,316 days.
missions.achievement: Confirmed Viking 1 results; returned 16,000 images and studied seasonal frost.

missions.name: Phobos 1
missions.story: Intended to study Mars and the moon Phobos; lost on the way due to a software command error.
missions.achievement: Tested new instruments before failure.

missions.name: Phobos 2
missions.currentLocation: Last known position near Phobos orbit
missions.story: Reached Mars orbit and returned data on the atmosphere and Phobos before contact was lost during the Phobos approach.
missions.achievement: Detected a faint dust ring around Mars and measured the Martian magnetic environment.

missions.name: Mars Global Surveyor
missions.currentLocation: Lost contact November 2006, remained in orbit
missions.story: Operated for nine years, systematically mapping Mars with cameras, laser altimeter and spectrometers.
missions.achievement: Produced definitive global maps; discovered gullies suggesting recent water flow; supported all subsequent Mars landers as a relay.

missions.name: Mars Pathfinder
missions.story: Delivered the first Mars rover (Sojourner) using airbags. Sojourner drove 100 m over 83 days.
missions.achievement: First rover on Mars; first airbag landing; demonstrated "faster, better, cheaper" planetary exploration.

missions.name: Mars Climate Orbiter
missions.story: Lost during orbit insertion due to a unit-conversion error between metric and imperial thrust data.
missions.achievement: Costly lesson in engineering units and team communication.

missions.name: Mars Polar Lander
missions.story: Lost during descent; a sensor fault is believed to have shut the engines early.
missions.achievement: Prompted programme reforms including the "follow the water" strategy.

missions.name: 2001 Mars Odyssey
missions.story: The longest-serving Mars orbiter, mapping mineralogy and serving as the primary communications relay for surface missions.
missions.achievement: Global mapping of water and ice; found widespread subsurface hydrogen; relayed data for every Mars rover since 2004.

missions.name: Mars Express
missions.story: Europe's first Mars mission; the lander Beagle 2 failed, but the orbiter has operated for over 20 years.
missions.achievement: Radar detection of buried polar ice and ancient lake beds; 3D atmospheric mapping; found methane hints; imaged Phobos in detail.

missions.name: Spirit (MER-A)
missions.currentLocation: Final location near Home Plate, Gusev crater (14.57°S, 175.47°E)
missions.story: Planned for 90 sols; operated for 2,210 sols, driving 7.73 km in Gusev crater.
missions.achievement: Evidence of ancient water-altered rocks; discovered the "Home Plate" volcanic plateau; got stuck in soft soil in 2009.

missions.name: Opportunity (MER-B)
missions.currentLocation: Final position in Perseverance Valley, Endeavour crater (2.28°S, 5.23°W)
missions.story: Operated for 5,111 sols and drove 45.16 km — the longest off-world drive until 2024 (Perseverance is near).
missions.achievement: Found strong evidence of ancient liquid water and the first meteorite on another planet; survived a planet-wide dust storm in 2007.

missions.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO)
missions.story: High-resolution imaging and climate monitoring from orbit, plus a crucial data-relay role for surface missions.
missions.achievement: HiRISE images at 30 cm per pixel; discovered recurring slope lineae; identified the landing sites used by Curiosity, InSight and Perseverance.

missions.name: Phoenix
missions.story: Landed in the Martian Arctic and dug into the ice-rich soil with a robotic arm.
missions.achievement: Confirmed water ice just below the surface; observed snowfall from clouds; analysed soil chemistry.

missions.name: Phobos-Grunt
missions.story: Intended to return a sample from Phobos; the upper stage failed to fire and the spacecraft was stranded in Earth orbit.
missions.achievement: The re-entry was tracked and yielded engineering lessons.

missions.name: Curiosity (Mars Science Laboratory)
missions.story: The largest rover on Mars, landed in Gale crater in August 2012 using a sky crane. Still exploring Mount Sharp.
missions.achievement: Discovered organic molecules in ancient lake sediments and that Gale crater was habitable; found methane spikes; measured radiation for human missions.

missions.name: MAVEN
missions.story: Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN, studying how Mars lost its atmosphere and water.
missions.achievement: Measured atmospheric escape rates; determined that solar wind stripped Mars's atmosphere; sampled the "flying" dust storms; science mission extended to 2026.

missions.name: Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission)
missions.currentLocation: Contact lost April 2022 after eight years; remains in Mars orbit
missions.story: India's first interplanetary mission, which reached Mars orbit on its first attempt and for a remarkably low cost.
missions.achievement: Demonstrated Mars orbit insertion on the first try; mapped methane and atmospheric composition; inspired India's deep-space programme.

missions.name: ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO)
missions.story: Studies atmospheric trace gases (especially methane) and acts as a data relay for Mars landers.
missions.achievement: Best measurements of methane and its isotopes on Mars, finding little active biological methane; mapped hydrogen to 1 m depth; relay for Rosalind Franklin.

missions.name: Schiaparelli
missions.story: Demonstration lander that crashed during descent when a gyroscope reading saturated and the parachute released early.
missions.achievement: Returned data that informed the redesign of the Rosalind Franklin landing system.

missions.name: InSight
missions.story: Interior Exploration using Seismic Investigations, Geodesy and Heat Transport — the first mission to study Mars's interior with a seismometer.
missions.achievement: Detected over 1,300 marsquakes, revealing a large liquid core and a crust thinner than expected; recorded the sound of wind and dust devils.

missions.name: Hope (Al-Amal)
missions.story: The Arab world's first interplanetary mission, entering Mars orbit in February 2021 on a large elliptical orbit.
missions.achievement: First complete picture of Mars's atmospheric dynamics across the day and seasons; discovered new auroral types.

missions.name: Tianwen-1
missions.workingNowText: Orbiter yes; Zhurong rover inactive (entered hibernation 2022)
missions.currentLocation: Orbiter in Mars orbit; lander in Utopia Planitia (25.1°N, 109.9°E)
missions.story: China's first Mars mission, which orbited, landed and deployed the Zhurong rover in a single mission.
missions.achievement: First Chinese Mars landing; first rover on Mars other than US rovers; orbiter mapping and communications relay.

missions.name: Perseverance
missions.currentLocation: Jezero crater, exploring the western fan and rim (roughly 18.44°N, 77.45°E)
missions.story: The flagship astrobiology rover, landed at Jezero crater in February 2021. It is collecting a sample cache for future return to Earth.
missions.achievement: First successful demonstration of producing oxygen on Mars (MOXIE); confirmed ancient lake sediments; caching 24+ samples; carrying the first Mars helicopter.

missions.name: Ingenuity
missions.currentLocation: Final resting place in Neretva Vallis, Jezero crater
missions.story: First powered aircraft to fly on another planet, completing 72 flights over three years.
missions.achievement: Proved controlled flight in a 1% atmosphere; scouted terrain for Perseverance; survived a 2023 communications blackout.

missions.name: ESCAPADE
missions.story: Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers — two small orbiters to study how Mars's magnetosphere interacts with the solar wind.
missions.achievement: First NASA science mission launched on New Glenn; planned to study atmospheric escape from a multi-point vantage.

missions.name: Rosalind Franklin
missions.story: Europe's ExoMars rover, carrying a 2 m drill to search for signs of past life below the sterilising radiation of the surface.
missions.achievement: Planned: first European Mars rover and deepest subsurface sampling on Mars.

missions.name: Mars Sample Return
missions.story: Planned campaign to retrieve the sample tubes cached by Perseverance and return them to Earth for analysis.
missions.achievement: Planned: the first Mars sample return, using an orbiter, a lander and a Mars ascent vehicle.

missions.name: Pioneer 10
missions.currentLocation: Interstellar space, heading toward the constellation Taurus
missions.story: First spacecraft to fly past Jupiter and the first to cross the asteroid belt.
missions.achievement: First close-up images of Jupiter; measured Jupiter's radiation belts and magnetic field; first spacecraft to achieve solar system escape velocity.

missions.name: Pioneer 11
missions.story: First spacecraft to fly past Saturn after a Jupiter encounter that used gravity assists to reach the ringed planet.
missions.achievement: Discovered Saturn's F ring; first close images of Saturn; first spacecraft to visit two giant planets.

missions.name: Voyager 1
missions.workingNowText: Yes — limited power, instruments being shut down progressively
missions.currentLocation: Interstellar space, more than 163 AU from the Sun and still moving outward
missions.story: Flew past Jupiter (1979) and Saturn (1980), then left the heliosphere in 2012. The most distant human-made object.
missions.achievement: Discovered volcanoes on Io and the Io plasma torus; detailed Saturn ring structure; returned the "Pale Blue Dot" image; entered interstellar space in 2012.

missions.name: Voyager 2
missions.currentLocation: Interstellar space, about 136 AU from the Sun
missions.story: The only spacecraft to visit all four giant planets — Jupiter (1979), Saturn (1981), Uranus (1986) and Neptune (1989).
missions.achievement: Discovered 10 Uranian moons and Neptune's Great Dark Spot; imaged Triton's geysers; entered interstellar space in 2018.

missions.name: Galileo
missions.story: First spacecraft to orbit Jupiter (1995), releasing a probe into the atmosphere. It also flew past asteroids Gaspra and Ida.
missions.achievement: Discovered evidence for subsurface oceans on Europa and Ganymede; found the first moon of an asteroid (Dactyl); direct atmospheric measurements.

missions.name: Ulysses
missions.story: Used a Jupiter flyby in 1992 to enter the first polar orbit around the Sun.
missions.achievement: First measurements of the Sun's polar regions; discovered that the solar wind is faster from the poles.

missions.name: Cassini (Jupiter flyby)
missions.story: Flew within 9.7 million km of Jupiter in December 2000, gathering data with Cassini and Huygens instruments.
missions.achievement: Produced a 26,000-image Jupiter movie; measured Jupiter's polar weather; coincident observations with Galileo.

missions.name: New Horizons (Jupiter flyby)
missions.currentLocation: Continued to Pluto and the Kuiper Belt
missions.story: Used a Jupiter gravity assist that cut three years off its Pluto voyage and gathered the best images of Jupiter since Galileo.
missions.achievement: First close-up images of Jupiter's Little Red Spot; measured Io's volcanoes and Jupiter's magnetotail.

missions.name: Juno
missions.currentLocation: Polar orbit around Jupiter (perijove about 4,200 km)
missions.story: In polar orbit around Jupiter since July 2016, peering below the cloud tops to study the planet's interior, magnetosphere and auroras.
missions.achievement: Measured Jupiter's deep zonal winds and its surprisingly fuzzy core; discovered cyclones at the poles; closest ever images of Io and Europa; mission extended to 2025 and beyond.

missions.name: JUICE
missions.currentLocation: Heliocentric cruise; Jupiter arrival 2031, Ganymede orbit 2034
missions.story: Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer, on a cruise to become the first spacecraft to orbit a moon other than Earth's Moon (Ganymede, 2034).
missions.achievement: Completed a Venus flyby in Aug 2024 and an Earth flyby in Aug 2025; first detection of a specific molecule at the surface of Ganymede.

missions.name: Europa Clipper
missions.currentLocation: Heliocentric cruise; currently outbound, approaching the inner solar system for its Earth flyby
missions.story: A flagship mission to assess whether Europa's subsurface ocean could support life, using about 50 close flybys.
missions.achievement: Completed a Mars gravity assist on 1 March 2025; Earth flyby scheduled December 2026; Jupiter arrival 2030.

missions.name: Pioneer 11 (Saturn flyby)
missions.story: First spacecraft to fly past Saturn, passing about 20,000 km above the cloud tops.
missions.achievement: Discovered the F ring; found a new ring and measured the planet's magnetic field and temperatures.

missions.name: Voyager 1 (Saturn flyby)
missions.story: Close Saturn encounter with a targeted approach to Titan, then flung out of the ecliptic plane.
missions.achievement: Detailed image of Titan's haze; discovered spokes in the B ring and new moons.

missions.name: Voyager 2 (Saturn flyby)
missions.story: Second Saturn encounter, passing 161,000 km from the cloud tops before continuing to Uranus.
missions.achievement: Discovered more ring spokes and moons; studied Saturn's atmosphere in detail.

missions.name: Cassini-Huygens
missions.currentLocation: Ended in the "Grand Finale", intentionally diving into Saturn's atmosphere to avoid contaminating moons.
missions.story: A 20-year mission (13 in orbit). It carried ESA's Huygens probe, which made the most distant landing ever, on Titan.
missions.achievement: Detected a global ocean under Enceladus's south pole with hydrothermal activity; found methane lakes on Titan; discovered six new moons; sustained a 13-year ring survey.

missions.name: Dragonfly
missions.story: A nuclear-powered rotorcraft that will fly between dozens of sites on Titan, sampling organic material and measuring habitability.
missions.achievement: Planned: first multi-site flying laboratory on another world; Titan's dense atmosphere makes powered flight easy.

missions.name: Voyager 2 (Uranus flyby)
missions.story: The only spacecraft ever to visit Uranus, passing 81,500 km from the cloud tops.
missions.achievement: Discovered 10 moons including Miranda's "coronae" cliffs and 2 new rings; measured a 42-year-long polar day and an offset magnetic field.

missions.name: Voyager 2 (Neptune flyby)
missions.story: The only spacecraft ever to visit Neptune, passing about 4,950 km above the north pole.
missions.achievement: Discovered the Great Dark Spot and the fastest winds in the Solar System (over 2,000 km/h); imaged geysers on Triton; found 6 new moons and complete ring arcs.

missions.name: New Horizons
missions.currentLocation: Deep in the Kuiper Belt, more than 60 AU from the Sun
missions.story: The first mission to Pluto, flying past on 14 July 2015 at 12,500 km, then on to Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth on 1 January 2019.
missions.achievement: Transformed knowledge of Pluto — nitrogen glaciers, a haze-layered atmosphere, the "heart" Sputnik Planitia; first close look at a Kuiper Belt object; now studying the outer heliosphere.

missions.name: ICE (International Cometary Explorer)
missions.story: Originally ISEE-3 studying the solar wind; repurposed to fly through the tail of comet Giacobini-Zinner in September 1985.
missions.achievement: First spacecraft to encounter a comet; measured the comet's plasma tail.

missions.name: Vega 1 (Halley flyby)
missions.story: After releasing a Venus balloon, it flew within 8,889 km of Halley's nucleus.
missions.achievement: First (with Vega 2 and Giotto) direct imaging of a comet nucleus; measured dust and gas.

missions.name: Giotto
missions.story: Flew within 596 km of Halley's nucleus, the closest of the 1986 armada.
missions.achievement: First true picture of a comet nucleus — a dark, potato-shaped body with jets; found the surface darker than coal.

missions.name: NEAR Shoemaker
missions.currentLocation: Landed on Eros, now dormant on the surface
missions.story: First spacecraft to orbit an asteroid (Eros, 2000) and the first to land on one (12 February 2001).
missions.achievement: Mapped Eros in detail; measured its composition, mass and magnetic field; transmitted from the surface for two weeks.

missions.name: Deep Space 1
missions.story: A technology demonstration mission that tested ion propulsion and autonomous navigation, then achieved both asteroid and comet encounters.
missions.achievement: Validated ion drive and AI-based navigation; returned the best images of comet Borrelly up to that time.

missions.name: Stardust
missions.workingNowText: No (mission ended; extended as Stardust-NExT to Tempel 1 in 2011)
missions.currentLocation: Sample returned; capsule at the Utah Test and Training Range
missions.story: Flew through the coma of Wild 2 in 2004 and returned samples to Earth in 2006.
missions.achievement: First comet samples returned to Earth; found amino acids and evidence that comets carry water-borne minerals.

missions.name: Hayabusa (MUSES-C)
missions.currentLocation: Sample returned to Earth; spacecraft burned up on re-entry
missions.story: Landed on Itokawa in 2005 and returned a capsule despite multiple failures, arriving back in 2010.
missions.achievement: First asteroid samples returned to Earth (about 1,500 grains); proved that S-type asteroids are rubble piles.

missions.name: Deep Impact
missions.currentLocation: Heliocentric orbit (extended as EPOXI to comet Hartley 2)
missions.story: Fired a 370 kg copper impactor into comet Tempel 1, creating a crater and a plume.
missions.achievement: First deliberate impact into a comet; revealed fine dust and ice beneath the surface; observed by many spacecraft and telescopes.

missions.name: Rosetta
missions.story: First mission to orbit a comet (2014) and to land a probe on one — Philae touched down on 12 November 2014.
missions.achievement: Discovered molecular oxygen, amino acids and water-ice on the comet; tracked the comet's activity through perihelion; revealed a "rubber duck" shape.

missions.name: Dawn
missions.target: Asteroid 4 Vesta and dwarf planet Ceres
missions.story: First spacecraft to orbit two different extraterrestrial bodies, arriving at Vesta in 2011 and Ceres in 2015.
missions.achievement: Found water-bearing minerals on Vesta; discovered bright carbonate deposits and organics on Ceres; revealed Ceres surface features from orbit.

missions.name: Hayabusa2
missions.currentLocation: Heliocentric orbit, en route to 1998 KY26
missions.story: Returned 5.4 g of Ryugu material to Earth in December 2020 and is now on an extended mission to asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031.
missions.achievement: First subsurface asteroid sample; found amino acids and water-bearing minerals; deployed rovers and an impactor.

missions.name: OSIRIS-REx / OSIRIS-APEX
missions.currentLocation: En route to asteroid Apophis, arriving 2029
missions.story: Touchdown on Bennu in 2020 returned 121.6 g of samples on 24 September 2023 — the largest asteroid sample ever. The spacecraft was renamed OSIRIS-APEX for a new target.
missions.achievement: Found water-bearing clays, carbon-rich material and amino acids in the sample; measured Bennu's "rubble pile" structure.

missions.name: Lucy
missions.currentLocation: Heliocentric orbit, touring the Trojan swarms
missions.story: The first mission to study the Jupiter Trojans, a fossil population from the Solar System's formation.
missions.achievement: Flew past asteroid Dinkinesh in November 2023, discovering a contact-binary moonlet; eight more targets through 2033.

missions.name: DART
missions.currentLocation: Impacted Dimorphos; remains as debris on the surface
missions.story: Double Asteroid Redirection Test — the first planetary defence mission, deliberately crashing into Dimorphos to change its orbit.
missions.achievement: Successfully shortened Dimorphos's orbital period by about 32 minutes, far exceeding requirements; validated kinetic impact deflection.

missions.name: Hera
missions.currentLocation: Heliocentric cruise toward the Didymos system
missions.story: Europe's follow-up to DART, to survey the impact crater and measure Dimorphos's mass and internal structure.
missions.achievement: Completed an Earth gravity assist in 2025; Mars flyby planned 2026; arrival at the Didymos system in late 2026.

missions.name: Psyche
missions.story: A mission to a metal-rich asteroid believed to be the exposed core of an early planetesimal.
missions.achievement: Completed a Mars gravity assist in May 2026; arrival at Psyche planned for 2029.

missions.name: Tianwen-2
missions.story: China's first asteroid sample-return mission, targeting a quasi-satellite of Earth, then flying on to a main-belt comet.
missions.achievement: Launched May 2025; planned sample return in 2027 and comet encounter around 2034.

missions.name: NEO Surveyor
missions.story: A dedicated infrared telescope to find, track and characterise at least two-thirds of potentially hazardous near-Earth objects larger than 140 m.
missions.achievement: Planned: the first purpose-built planetary defence space telescope.

missions.name: Comet Interceptor
missions.story: A "waiting" spacecraft parked at L2 that will redirect to fly past a dynamically new comet entering the inner Solar System.
missions.achievement: Planned: the first mission to a pristine, never-before-visited comet.

missions.name: Pioneer 6
missions.story: Part of the Pioneer solar weather network, operating for more than 35 years.
missions.achievement: First long-duration solar wind and interplanetary magnetic field monitoring.

missions.name: Helios 1
missions.story: First non-Soviet spacecraft to reach perihelion inside Mercury's orbit (0.29 AU).
missions.achievement: Measured the solar wind and cosmic rays closer to the Sun than ever before.

missions.name: Helios 2
missions.story: Deeper perihelion of 0.29 AU and higher data rate than Helios 1.
missions.achievement: Measured the solar wind's temperature, speed and magnetic structure near the Sun.

missions.name: Ulysses
missions.story: The first spacecraft to orbit over the Sun's poles, using a Jupiter gravity assist.
missions.achievement: Discovered the fast polar solar wind; showed that cosmic rays arrive from all directions; mapped the heliosphere's 3D shape.

missions.name: SOHO
missions.story: Solar and Heliospheric Observatory, stationed at the Sun-Earth L1 point, continuously watching the Sun for nearly 30 years.
missions.achievement: Discovered thousands of comets (the most prolific comet discoverer ever); continuous solar monitoring; the source of most space-weather imagery.

missions.name: Wind
missions.story: One of the longest-serving heliophysics missions, measuring the solar wind upstream of Earth.
missions.achievement: Provided key data on solar wind composition and the magnetosphere's response; also flew past the Moon early in its mission.

missions.name: ACE
missions.story: Advanced Composition Explorer, measuring energetic particles and the solar wind from L1.
missions.achievement: Provides real-time solar wind alerts used for space-weather forecasting; determined the composition of solar and galactic material.

missions.name: Genesis
missions.currentLocation: Sample capsule crashed in Utah; samples recovered from the wreckage
missions.story: Collected solar wind particles on ultra-pure wafers and returned them to Earth, though the parachute failed.
missions.achievement: First samples of solar wind returned (from the crash debris); provided oxygen-isotope measurements of the Sun.

missions.name: STEREO
missions.currentLocation: STEREO-A in heliocentric orbit; STEREO-B lost 2014
missions.story: Twin spacecraft (A and B) providing stereoscopic 3D views of the Sun from opposite sides.
missions.achievement: First 3D images of the Sun and coronal mass ejections; STEREO-A provided unique far-side views; B lost contact in 2014.

missions.name: Hinode
missions.story: Solar-B mission studying the Sun's magnetic field, corona and chromosphere in high resolution.
missions.achievement: Measured the Sun's magnetic field with unprecedented precision; observed chromospheric jets and waves.

missions.name: Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO)
missions.story: The most detailed and continuous solar observatory, returning an image every 0.75 seconds.
missions.achievement: Its iconic extreme-ultraviolet images underpin solar science and public understanding; tracked the solar cycle from minimum to maximum.

missions.name: Parker Solar Probe
missions.currentLocation: Highly elliptical heliocentric orbit, repeatedly diving close to the Sun
missions.story: The first mission to "touch" the Sun, flying through the corona. On 24 December 2024 it passed 6.1 million km from the Sun's surface at 692,000 km/h — the fastest human-made object ever.
missions.achievement: First in-situ measurements inside the corona; discovered magnetic switchbacks; explained the corona's heat and the origin of the fast solar wind.

missions.name: Solar Orbiter
missions.story: A joint mission combining close-up solar imaging with the first views of the Sun's polar regions.
missions.achievement: First images of the Sun's polar regions; linked coronal jets to the solar wind; coordinated observations with Parker Solar Probe.

missions.name: Aditya-L1
missions.story: India's first dedicated solar observatory, operating from the Sun-Earth L1 point.
missions.achievement: Studying the corona, solar wind and space weather; first Indian solar mission.

missions.name: IMAP
missions.story: Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe, mapping the boundary of the heliosphere where interstellar material meets the solar wind.
missions.achievement: Studying cosmic-ray acceleration and the heliosphere's interaction with the interstellar medium.

missions.name: PUNCH
missions.story: Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere — four small satellites creating 3D images of the Sun's corona and solar wind.
missions.achievement: First mission to image the entire inner heliosphere continuously in 3D.

missions.name: TRACERS
missions.story: Tandem Reconnection and Cusp Electrodynamics Reconnaissance Satellites, studying magnetic reconnection above Earth's poles.
missions.achievement: Studying how solar activity disrupts Earth's magnetic field to improve space-weather prediction.

missions.name: Cluster
missions.currentLocation: Four spacecraft re-entered the atmosphere in September 2024
missions.story: Four identical spacecraft flying in formation to map Earth's magnetosphere in 3D.
missions.achievement: Revealed the fine structure of the magnetopause and magnetic reconnection; the first multi-scale magnetospheric observatory.

missions.name: Hubble Space Telescope
missions.workingNowText: Yes — operating on three gyros, degraded but functional
missions.story: The most productive observatory in history, in low Earth orbit since 1990 and serviced five times by Shuttle crews.
missions.achievement: Measured the expansion rate of the Universe; helped discover dark energy; the Deep Field images; contributed to the first exoplanet atmosphere detections.

missions.name: Compton Gamma Ray Observatory
missions.story: One of NASA's four Great Observatories, surveying the gamma-ray sky.
missions.achievement: Produced the first all-sky gamma-ray map; discovered gamma-ray bursts' isotropic distribution; catalogued 2,704 sources.

missions.name: Chandra X-ray Observatory
missions.story: The most powerful X-ray telescope ever built, in a highly elliptical Earth orbit for over 25 years.
missions.achievement: Imaged the first X-ray emission from a black hole binary; revealed dark matter in galaxy clusters; observed supernova remnants and pulsars.

missions.name: XMM-Newton
missions.story: Europe's flagship X-ray observatory, with the largest X-ray telescope mirrors ever flown.
missions.achievement: Discovered evidence of the "missing baryons"; studied black hole spin and galaxy cluster dynamics.

missions.name: Spitzer Space Telescope
missions.story: The fourth Great Observatory, observing in infrared from a trailing Earth orbit.
missions.achievement: Detected the light of exoplanets; found a seven-planet system (TRAPPIST-1); measured the Universe's oldest galaxies; imaged Saturn's largest ring.

missions.name: Swift
missions.story: A rapid-response gamma-ray burst observatory that slews to bursts within seconds.
missions.achievement: Determined the origin of short gamma-ray bursts; detected the first gravitational-wave counterpart; discovered the most distant GRB.

missions.name: Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope
missions.story: The most sensitive gamma-ray observatory, studying pulsars, blazars and dark matter.
missions.achievement: Catalogued thousands of gamma-ray sources; discovered gravitational-wave event counterparts; mapped the Milky Way's gamma-ray glow.

missions.name: Kepler
missions.story: Revolutionised exoplanet science by staring at 150,000 stars to detect planetary transits.
missions.achievement: Confirmed more than 2,700 exoplanets; showed Earth-sized planets are common; survived two reaction-wheel failures using solar pressure.

missions.name: Gaia
missions.currentLocation: Sun-Earth L2; ended observations January 2025 after 11 years
missions.story: The most precise astrometric survey ever, measuring positions, distances and motions of nearly two billion stars.
missions.achievement: Created a 3D map of the Milky Way; discovered it merged with a galaxy 10 billion years ago; catalogued hundreds of thousands of asteroids.

missions.name: TESS
missions.story: Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, scanning almost the entire sky for new planets around bright nearby stars.
missions.achievement: Discovered thousands of planet candidates; found planets around nearby stars suitable for atmospheric study; discovered comet-like tails on exoplanets.

missions.name: CHEOPS
missions.story: CHaracterising ExOPlanet Satellite, measuring the sizes of known exoplanets precisely.
missions.achievement: Refined planetary radii; characterised the first exoplanet with a ring system (HIP 41378 f); studied exoplanet atmospheres.

missions.name: James Webb Space Telescope
missions.currentLocation: Sun-Earth L2 Lagrange point, about 1.5 million km from Earth
missions.story: The largest and most powerful space telescope, operating in the infrared from the Sun-Earth L2 point.
missions.achievement: Observed the earliest galaxies within 300 million years of the Big Bang; detected CO2 and water in exoplanet atmospheres; transformed studies of star formation and Solar System objects.

missions.name: Euclid
missions.story: Mapping the geometry of the dark Universe by surveying billions of galaxies.
missions.achievement: First science release in 2025 revealed hundreds of millions of objects and new gravitational lenses; building the largest 3D map of the Universe.

missions.name: IXPE
missions.story: Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer, the first mission to measure X-ray polarisation from cosmic sources.
missions.achievement: Mapped the polarisation of pulsars, black hole accrete disks and supernova remnants; found polarisation from the Crab Nebula with a surprising geometry.

missions.name: NuSTAR
missions.story: The first focusing high-energy X-ray telescope in orbit.
missions.achievement: Measured black hole spin; mapped radioactive titanium in supernova remnants; discovered high-energy X-ray flares from the Sun.

missions.name: XRISM
missions.story: X-Ray Imaging and Spectroscopy Mission, a next-generation X-ray observatory using a microcalorimeter.
missions.achievement: Returned unprecedented X-ray spectra of galaxy clusters, supernova remnants and black holes.

missions.name: INTEGRAL
missions.story: International Gamma-Ray Astrophysics Laboratory, studying the gamma-ray sky for over 20 years.
missions.achievement: Mapped the 511 keV positron annihilation emission from the galaxy's centre; discovered many gamma-ray sources.

missions.name: Spektr-RG
missions.story: Russian-German X-ray observatory, including eROSITA, which surveyed the whole sky in X-rays.
missions.achievement: First all-sky X-ray maps from L2; discovered hundreds of thousands of new sources; eROSITA was placed in safe mode in 2022.

missions.name: Planck
missions.story: Measured the cosmic microwave background with unprecedented precision from L2.
missions.achievement: Produced the best map of the infant Universe; refined the age (13.8 billion years) and composition of the cosmos.

missions.name: Herschel
missions.story: The largest infrared telescope ever flown, observing from L2.
missions.achievement: Discovered water in star-forming clouds and exoplanet atmospheres; traced star formation across cosmic time.

missions.name: WISE / NEOWISE
missions.currentLocation: Deorbited and burned up in Earth's atmosphere on 1 November 2024
missions.story: Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer mapped the sky in infrared; repurposed as NEOWISE to hunt asteroids.
missions.achievement: Catalogued hundreds of millions of objects; discovered 3,000+ near-Earth objects; provided the foundational infrared all-sky map.

missions.name: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
missions.story: A wide-field infrared observatory with the same mirror size as Hubble but 100 times the field of view.
missions.achievement: Planned: survey dark energy, discover thousands of exoplanets via microlensing, and test the first coronagraph.

missions.name: PLATO
missions.story: PLAnetary Transits and Oscillations of stars, to find and characterise Earth-sized planets in habitable zones.
missions.achievement: Planned: long-duration monitoring of bright stars to measure planet masses and ages.

missions.name: ARIEL
missions.story: Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large-survey, to survey the atmospheres of about 1,000 exoplanets.
missions.achievement: Planned: the first large-scale chemical census of exoplanet atmospheres.

missions.name: Landsat 1
missions.story: The first civil Earth-resources satellite, beginning the longest-running continuous record of Earth's land surface.
missions.achievement: Established the multi-decade Landsat record used for agriculture, forestry and land-change science.

missions.name: Landsat 8
missions.story: Continues the Landsat record with improved radiometry and new coastal/aerosol bands.
missions.achievement: Key data source for global land-cover change, water use and crop monitoring.

missions.name: Landsat 9
missions.story: Latest Landsat, flying in formation with Landsat 8 to image the whole Earth every eight days.
missions.achievement: Extends the 50-year Landsat record for climate and land-use science.

missions.name: Terra
missions.story: Flagship Earth Observing System satellite carrying ASTER, CERES, MISR, MODIS and MOPITT.
missions.achievement: Two decades of global climate records including aerosols, clouds, fires and vegetation.

missions.name: Aqua
missions.story: EOS satellite focused on the water cycle, carrying AIRS, AMSR-E and MODIS.
missions.achievement: Critical for weather forecasting (AIRS) and the global water and carbon cycles.

missions.name: Aura
missions.story: EOS atmospheric chemistry mission measuring ozone, aerosols and trace gases.
missions.achievement: Provided the definitive record of the ozone hole's recovery; tracked air quality globally.

missions.name: ICESat-2
missions.story: Laser altimeter measuring changes in Earth's ice sheets, sea ice and vegetation height.
missions.achievement: Precise measurement of ice-sheet loss in Greenland and Antarctica; sea-ice thickness trends.

missions.name: GRACE-FO
missions.story: Twin satellites measuring Earth's gravity field to track water movement.
missions.achievement: Tracks groundwater depletion, ice loss and sea-level change by weighing the planet monthly.

missions.name: Jason-3
missions.story: Ocean altimetry mission continuing the long sea-level record.
missions.achievement: Precise global sea-level measurements showing an accelerating rise.

missions.name: SWOT
missions.story: Surface Water and Ocean Topography, the first global survey of Earth's surface water.
missions.achievement: Measures the height of water in lakes, rivers and oceans; detected previously unmapped small water bodies.

missions.name: Sentinel-2
missions.story: High-resolution multispectral imaging for the Copernicus programme.
missions.achievement: The workhorse of European land monitoring, used for agriculture, forestry and disaster response.

missions.name: Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich
missions.story: Continues the precise sea-level record into the 2030s.
missions.achievement: Measures global sea level to within a few centimetres, tracking the rate of rise.

missions.name: EarthCARE
missions.story: Earth Cloud, Aerosol and Radiation Explorer, measuring clouds and aerosols with a lidar and radar together.
missions.achievement: First mission to measure cloud profiles and aerosols simultaneously, improving climate models.

missions.name: PACE
missions.story: Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, ocean Ecosystem, measuring ocean colour and atmospheric particles.
missions.achievement: Tracking ocean ecosystems and harmful algal blooms from space.

missions.name: GOES-19 (GOES-U)
missions.story: The latest geostationary weather satellite, monitoring the Atlantic and eastern US.
missions.achievement: Continuous severe-weather monitoring; first GOES with a compact coronagraph for space weather.

missions.name: International Space Station
missions.workingNowText: Yes — operating, with retirement expected around 2030
missions.currentLocation: Low Earth orbit, about 400 km altitude, 51.6° inclination
missions.story: Continuously crewed since 2 November 2000 and the largest structure ever assembled in space, with over 270 visitors from 21 countries.
missions.achievement: Thousands of experiments in biology, physics, medicine and Earth observation; the only long-duration microgravity laboratory; landmark of international cooperation.

stations.name: Salyut 1
stations.story: The world's first space station. The Soyuz 11 crew spent 23 days aboard, a record at the time, but died during re-entry when a valve opened.
stations.achievement: Proved long-duration habitation was possible; conducted astronomy, Earth observation and medical studies.

stations.name: Salyut 2 (Almaz OPS-1)
stations.story: The first Almaz military station, which lost pressurisation shortly after launch and was never crewed.
stations.achievement: An early attempt at a military reconnaissance station.

stations.name: Skylab
stations.story: America's first space station, built from a converted Saturn V upper stage. Hosted three crews for 28, 59 and 84 days.
stations.achievement: First US long-duration spaceflight; solar astronomy; Earth resources; proved humans could live and work in orbit long-term.

stations.name: Salyut 3 (Almaz OPS-2)
stations.story: Second Almaz station; one crew visited briefly and tested a 23 mm cannon successfully.
stations.achievement: Military reconnaissance tests and the first use of a defensive gun in orbit.

stations.name: Salyut 4
stations.story: First successful civilian station after Salyut 1, hosting two crews with stays of 30 and 63 days.
stations.achievement: Solar astronomy with the OST-1 telescope; materials experiments.

stations.name: Salyut 5 (Almaz OPS-3)
stations.story: Last Almaz station to be crewed, with two crews over 67 days.
stations.achievement: Military reconnaissance; conducted a 12-day cardiovascular study.

stations.name: Salyut 6
stations.story: First station with two docking ports, allowing cargo resupply by Progress and long stays. Crewed for 683 days total.
stations.achievement: Record long-duration flights; the first Progress cargo deliveries; international crews including Interkosmos astronauts.

stations.name: Salyut 7
stations.story: The last Salyut, hosting 6 crews and visited by both Soyuz and Progress. Famous for the 1985 rescue mission after total power loss.
stations.achievement: Record EVAs; the dramatic in-orbit repair of a dead station; modular expansion tests that informed Mir.

stations.name: Mir
stations.orbit: Deorbited into the Pacific Ocean in March 2001
stations.story: The first modular space station, built up over a decade with seven modules. Continuously occupied for almost 10 years (3,644 days), a record broken only by the ISS.
stations.achievement: Long-duration human spaceflight records; the Shuttle-Mir programme; landmark international cooperation; foundational science for the ISS.

stations.name: International Space Station (ISS)
stations.orbit: Low Earth orbit at about 400-420 km, 51.6° inclination
stations.story: The largest international space project in history, continuously crewed since 2 November 2000 and orbiting above 400 km.
stations.achievement: A continuously inhabited outpost for over 25 years; thousands of experiments; the first commercial crew and private astronaut missions; international diplomacy in orbit.

stations.name: Tiangong-1
stations.story: China's first space station, visited by two crewed Shenzhou missions including the first Chinese woman in space.
stations.achievement: Prototype for modular stations; verified life support and docking.

stations.name: Tiangong-2
stations.story: Improved single-module laboratory that hosted one 30-day crewed mission.
stations.achievement: Tested refuelling, life support and many microgravity experiments; the precursor to the permanent Tiangong station.

stations.name: Tiangong (Chinese Space Station)
stations.orbit: Low Earth orbit at about 340-450 km, 41.5° inclination
stations.story: China's permanent modular station, completed in 2022 with the Tianhe core and Wentian and Mengtian labs. About 180 t and 110 m³ habitable volume.
stations.achievement: Continuously crewed since 2022 with overlapping Shenzhou rotations; hundreds of experiments; independent human spaceflight capability.

stations.name: Genesis I
stations.story: The first expandable (inflatable) habitat in orbit, launched as a private technology test.
stations.achievement: Proved inflatable module technology, later used in a proposed NASA lunar habitat concept.

stations.name: Genesis II
stations.story: Second expandable habitat test with more interior volume and a life support test.
stations.achievement: Validated long-duration inflatable structures in orbit.

stations.name: BEAM
stations.story: The Bigelow Expandable Activity Module, attached to the ISS and inflated in May 2016.
stations.achievement: The first human-rated expandable habitat; demonstrated radiation and debris shielding over years on the ISS.

stations.name: Axiom Station
stations.story: A commercial station being built up from modules attached to the ISS, which will separate into an independent station when the ISS retires.
stations.achievement: Planned: the first commercial space station and the successor to ISS-era research.

stations.name: Starlab
stations.story: A commercial free-flying station designed as an ISS successor for research and manufacturing.
stations.achievement: Planned: a large single-launch station with a docking node and a robotic arm.

stations.name: Orbital Reef
stations.story: A commercially developed "business park in space" intended as a mixed-use orbital destination.
stations.achievement: Planned: modular infrastructure for research, tourism and manufacturing.

rockets.name: V-2 (Aggregat 4)
rockets.story: The first ballistic missile and the first human-made object to reach space (a 1942 test flight reached 206 km).
rockets.notableMissions: First rocket to cross the boundary of space; its engineers and design formed the basis of both US and Soviet rocketry after the Second World War.

rockets.name: R-7 / Sputnik
rockets.story: The world's first intercontinental ballistic missile, adapted to launch Sputnik 1 and Yuri Gagarin.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched Sputnik 1, Sputnik 2, Vostok 1 and early Luna missions; the ancestor of the Soyuz family still flying today.

rockets.name: Soyuz-FG
rockets.story: The workhorse crewed launcher of the 2000s and 2010s, with a flawless crewed record.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched every ISS crew between 2002 and 2019, plus Progress cargo and many commercial satellites.

rockets.name: Soyuz-2 (2.1a / 2.1b)
rockets.story: The current Russian workhorse, used for crewed launches, Progress, OneWeb and many commercial payloads.
rockets.notableMissions: Crewed launches to the ISS since 2020; launches of Europe's Galileo satellites; very high launch rate.

rockets.name: Saturn IB
rockets.story: Two-stage rocket used for Apollo Earth-orbit test flights, Skylab crews and the Apollo-Soyuz mission.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched the first crewed Apollo flight (Apollo 7), all three Skylab crews and the Apollo-Soyuz Test Project.

rockets.name: Saturn V
rockets.story: The most powerful rocket ever to fly successfully, with 13 launches and no crew lost. It sent humans to the Moon.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched all 24 Apollo astronauts who went to the Moon and placed Skylab in orbit; its F-1 engines remain the most powerful single-chamber engines ever flown.

rockets.name: N1
rockets.story: The Soviet answer to the Saturn V, with 30 first-stage engines. All four test flights failed, ending the Soviet crewed lunar programme.
rockets.notableMissions: Significant propulsion and control lessons, but never successful.

rockets.name: Energia
rockets.story: A super-heavy launcher that could carry the Buran spaceplane. It flew only twice.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched the Polyus payload and the Buran orbiter, which flew uncrewed and landed automatically.

rockets.name: Proton-K
rockets.story: The main Soviet heavy launcher for decades, launching space stations, planetary probes and modules.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched Salyut, Mir and ISS modules and the Luna, Venera, Mars and Phobos missions.

rockets.name: Proton-M
rockets.story: The modernised Proton, used for large commercial and government satellites and ISS modules.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched the Nauka ISS module, ExoMars TGO and many geostationary satellites.

rockets.name: Titan IIIE
rockets.story: A short-lived but historically important launcher, used for the Viking and Voyager missions.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched both Viking Mars missions and both Voyager probes.

rockets.name: Titan IV
rockets.story: The largest expendable US launcher of its era, used for national security and NASA payloads.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched the Cassini-Huygens mission to Saturn in 1997.

rockets.name: Space Shuttle
rockets.story: The first partially reusable orbital launch system, flying 135 missions over 30 years with five orbiters.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched and serviced Hubble; built the ISS; deployed Galileo, Magellan and Ulysses.

rockets.name: Delta II
rockets.story: The most reliable US launch vehicle of its era, with 155 flights and a 98.7% success rate.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched Mars Global Surveyor, both Mars Exploration Rovers, Phoenix, Dawn and Kepler.

rockets.name: Delta IV Heavy
rockets.story: A triple-core heavy launcher with a distinctive fireball at ignition, used for the largest national security payloads.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched the Parker Solar Probe and Orion's first test flight.

rockets.name: Atlas V
rockets.story: One of the most reliable rockets ever, with over 100 consecutive successful launches and a remarkable range of missions.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched New Horizons, Juno, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, Curiosity, Perseverance, LRO and many national security payloads.

rockets.name: Vulcan Centaur
rockets.story: ULA's next-generation launcher, replacing Atlas V and Delta IV, using Blue Origin BE-4 engines.
rockets.notableMissions: Its first flight carried the Peregrine lunar lander; designated to launch most future US national security missions.

rockets.name: Ariane 1
rockets.story: The first Ariane rocket, which gave Europe independent access to space.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched Giotto to Halley's Comet and many early European satellites.

rockets.name: Ariane 4
rockets.story: A highly successful commercial launcher, flying 116 times with a 97% success rate.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched hundreds of commercial communications satellites and European science missions.

rockets.name: Ariane 5
rockets.story: For two decades the dominant commercial heavy launcher, flying 117 times.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched Rosetta, Herschel, Planck, Gaia, BepiColombo, JUICE and JWST, and ATV cargo ships to the ISS.

rockets.name: Ariane 6
rockets.story: Europe's new workhorse, designed to cut launch costs and fly up to 12 times a year.
rockets.notableMissions: Its maiden flight in July 2024 reached orbit with a partial upper-stage anomaly; now Europe's primary launcher.

rockets.name: Vega-C
rockets.story: Europe's lightweight launcher for Earth observation and small science missions.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched many Sentinel satellites and European Earth-observation payloads.

rockets.name: Falcon 9
rockets.story: The most-flown rocket of the 2020s and the first orbital booster routinely reflown; many boosters have flown 20+ times.
rockets.notableMissions: Dominated the commercial launch market; launched Crew Dragon, thousands of Starlink satellites, DART, Euclid and IMAP.

rockets.name: Falcon Heavy
rockets.story: The most powerful operational rocket before Starship, made of three Falcon 9 cores.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched the Falcon Heavy test flight, Europa Clipper, Psyche and numerous national security payloads.

rockets.name: Starship
rockets.story: A fully reusable super-heavy system designed to carry 100+ tonnes, and the lander for NASA's Artemis III Moon landing.
rockets.notableMissions: Achieved the first booster catch with the launch tower in October 2024; it is the largest rocket ever flown.

rockets.name: New Glenn
rockets.story: Blue Origin's orbital-class reusable rocket, named after John Glenn, which reached orbit on its first flight.
rockets.notableMissions: Its first flight carried the Blue Ring pathfinder; its second launched NASA's ESCAPADE to Mars in November 2025.

rockets.name: Electron
rockets.story: The most-flown small dedicated launcher, with a unique electric-pump engine and first-stage recovery.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched CAPSTONE to the Moon and many smallsat missions; pioneered routine dedicated small launches.

rockets.name: Neutron
rockets.story: A reusable medium-lift rocket with a unique "Hungry Hippo" fairing and a recoverable first stage.
rockets.notableMissions: Planned: to compete with Falcon 9 for constellation and government launches.

rockets.name: H-IIA
rockets.story: Japan's highly reliable workhorse launcher, with a near-perfect record.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched Hayabusa2, Akatsuki, Kaguya, Hope (UAE Mars mission), SLIM and XRISM.

rockets.name: H3
rockets.story: Japan's next-generation launcher, designed to halve costs and fly more frequently, after a failed first flight.
rockets.notableMissions: Successfully flew in 2024 and now handles Japan's domestic and science launches.

rockets.name: PSLV
rockets.story: India's dependable workhorse, with over 60 flights and the record of launching 104 satellites on a single flight.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched Chandrayaan-1, Mangalyaan, Astrosat and Aditya-L1.

rockets.name: GSLV Mk II
rockets.story: India's cryogenic upper-stage launcher, which gives it geostationary capability.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched GSAT communication satellites and Chandrayaan-2.

rockets.name: LVM3 (GSLV Mk III)
rockets.story: India's most powerful rocket, which carried Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3, and commercial OneWeb satellites.

rockets.name: Long March 2F
rockets.story: China's only crewed launcher, used for every Shenzhou flight since 1999.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched all Shenzhou crewed missions and the Tiangong-1 and Tiangong-2 laboratories.

rockets.name: Long March 3B
rockets.story: China's workhorse for geostationary and lunar missions.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched Chang'e 1-4, Tianwen-2 and many Beidou and communications satellites.

rockets.name: Long March 5
rockets.story: China's most powerful rocket, which enabled its Mars and lunar sample-return missions.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched Tianwen-1, Chang'e 5 and Chang'e 6.

rockets.name: Long March 5B
rockets.story: A variant of Long March 5 designed to lift space-station modules, without an upper stage.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched the Tianhe core module and the Wentian and Mengtian labs — all three Tiangong station modules.

rockets.name: Long March 9
rockets.story: China's planned super-heavy launcher for lunar and Mars exploration, comparable in class to the Saturn V and Starship.
rockets.notableMissions: Planned: to support Chinese crewed lunar landing and deep-space ambitions.

rockets.name: Antares
rockets.story: A US launcher designed for the Cygnus ISS cargo resupply vehicle.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched Cygnus cargo ships to the ISS for a decade before retirement.

rockets.name: Pegasus XL
rockets.story: An air-launched rocket dropped from an L-1011 aircraft, giving flexible orbital access.
rockets.notableMissions: Launched NuSTAR and many small science satellites from the air.

rockets.name: Angara A5
rockets.story: Russia's new modular heavy launcher intended to replace Proton.
rockets.notableMissions: Flew test missions from Plesetsk and Vostochny; intended for future crewed use.
